e: The Merge into main branch chooser now offers a Not updated with main filter based on default-branch Git ancestry, keeping diverged branches that already contain main out of the stale results and localizing the chip in English, Hong Kong-style Cantonese, and bilingual mode
Ordinary Windows CI manual dispatches are cloud-only again: the temporary runner selector is removed, every job uses literal windows-2022, and self-hosted pools remain exclusive to Super Express
Linux CI now validates the packaged TUI changelog catalog against complete Git history, and generated catalog copy accurately identifies tag and referenced-entry commit timestamps

The packaged changelog tests now validate catalog arithmetic and exported release labels instead of freezing an old entry count, timestamp, and first commit that change whenever the generated history advances
Every ordinary Windows CI trigger now stays on clean GitHub-hosted runners with no manual self-hosted escape hatch, while Super Express retains its dedicated local runner pools
The generated parity contract now includes Settings tab docking as desktop feature 207, so Linux packaging no longer stops at the stale 206-row declaration

Every Super Express job, including the direct Windows release publisher, now stays on the registered self-hosted Windows and Linux pools, while ordinary CI and tested Express remain on GitHub-hosted runners
Ordinary Windows and Linux CI plus tested Express Release now use clean GitHub-hosted runners again, while only the three Super Express emergency workflows stay on their dedicated self-hosted pools

Unit tests no longer inherit a workflow-wide 4 GiB heap that made the memory-aware harness underestimate every worker, and Windows installer smoke now has a bounded 300-second wait with scoped late-process cleanup

Cloud-gate regressions now cover CodeMirror accessibility, complete Settings search and command-palette destinations, generated changelog and screenshot catalogs, Copilot policy intent, lazy-section inventory, and unique native-menu access keys

The Linux Python 3.13 TUI check now runs non-UI tests together and each UI test file in a fresh interpreter, preserving all coverage while preventing Textual native syntax state from carrying a segfault into the next app-heavy file

Self-hosted dependency setup still installs every declared package but no longer registers actions/cache, setup-uv, or setup-node archive-cache post hooks, so a completed build does not leave its runner busy with cleanup - 255eb9de1c

Windows native dependency setup now repairs arm64 before ClangCL, keeps both checks on one Visual Studio instance, verifies x64 MSVC and MSBuild, polls arm64 files after a quiet install, and uses an installer path format accepted across Visual Studio versions - 87ec5b3452

Self-hosted Windows dependency setup now waits for Visual Studio to materialize the verified x64 or arm64 ClangCL compiler and MSBuild toolset after the quiet installer returns, instead of declaring a still-running install broken - b5e6b7f825

Trusted CI, Express Release, and Super Express now target the registered local Windows and WSL runners with explicit labels, so incomplete alternate self-hosted machines cannot claim release jobs - c3cf40d0af

Self-hosted Windows dependency setup no longer passes the unsupported --wait option to Visual Studio Installer 4.7.25, so ClangCL bootstrap can reach dependency installation instead of failing before the app build - 28d7d032ef

The self-hosted release gate no longer depends on a separate jq executable: gh's built-in evaluator returns the sibling CI status, conclusion, and timestamp without a missing-runner-tool crash - ff0881d9d4

A fresh Windows dependency install now completes with the pinned TypeScript compiler, compiles the script's shared app imports, and lets the production renderer reach packaging

Settings > Accounts now uses one global active identity across GitHub.com, Enterprise, GitLab, and Bitbucket sections, so a cross-provider switch exposes Make active and never leaves two rows marked Active
Making an account active now also applies it to the selected same-host GitHub repository before its next authenticated operation, while preserving other repository and provider bindings

Transfer repository now lets you choose another signed-in GitHub account or organization, keep the existing name or choose a custom one, publish every local branch and tag or one clean snapshot commit, and retarget origin only after the destination is verified

A known-private source repository now keeps its destination private unless the user changes that choice, and transfer verification compares the destination branch with the exact pushed commit before origin is retargeted
Global Settings, Repository Settings, and Stash Manager now share browser-style page tabs with open, close, search, overflow, keyboard, and repository-scoped persistence

Release history lists every recorded release and its entries inside the app, searchable, filterable by category and date range, and readable with no network connection

The landing page and every rendered documentation page load the site's interactive features, including the dim sum surprise, which previously appeared on neither
Release entries show a 24-hour time beside the date wherever the release tag recorded one, and a release with no tag still says its date is unrecorded rather than showing a guess
The documentation site loads its changelog data when that tab is opened rather than making every visitor wait for it before the first page appears
Every screenshot in the gallery gets its own documentation page with working search, theme, language, and appearance controls
The cancel confirmation for a workflow run offers a Force cancel option for runs that ignore an ordinary cancellation, and says which kind was sent

The built-in browser renders the page instead of opening to a blank area below its toolbar and address bar

Text in the repository releases pane is legibly sized, including the release dates, status badges, asset digests and the filter-mode buttons
Web links open in the system browser by default, an explicit choice of the built-in browser survives a profile restore, and a link that fails to open reports it instead of doing nothing
Moving a tab into a group opens a searchable, keyboard-operable chooser instead of a context menu that grew with every group
The window close, minimize and maximize buttons stay on screen at narrow widths instead of being pushed past the right edge
The Windows title bar keeps a dedicated drag area, so the window can be moved by its top edge again
Choosing an organization when publishing a repository uses a searchable, keyboard-complete list that no longer hides choices or overflows a narrow dialog
The Sync repositories dialog can merge reviewed branches into the main branch, push without forcing, and remove local branches and worktrees only after proving each one is already contained remotely
Turning on Cheap LFS cloud compression for a confirmed private repository now actually publishes its workflow instead of preparing one that never ran

Merge conflicts can be handed to a local Codex or OpenCode session straight from the conflicts dialog, with the branches and conflicted files already described in the prompt

Cheap LFS restore progress details can be collapsed and expanded instead of always occupying the full panel
The command palette can now reach conflict repair, CI repair, showing or hiding background progress, and toggling Cheap LFS restore details

Logs can optionally be sent to a self-hosted diagnostic server with credentials redacted on both ends, while local-only logging stays the default and a slow or unreachable server never holds up the app

Closing Desktop Material on Windows waits for pending settings and profile history writes to finish instead of quitting mid-write
Cancelling a quit or window close returns the app to a fully usable state rather than leaving it half shut down

The releases view search filter, case, and regex builder buttons now fit inside the search field in short, narrow windows and at high zoom
Right-clicking a tab, a repository row, or a diff opens that surface's own context menu again, with Shift+right-click reserved for the appearance editor
Removing a repository also clears its saved large-file encryption password from the operating system credential store

The New and Edit tab group dialogs open as proper centered dialogs instead of being laid out inside the tab strip, where toolbar buttons painted over the group colour swatches

A tab group holding a single tab reads "1 tab" in its dropdown and in what screen readers announce, instead of "1 tabs"

Links and provider sign-in prompts open in a built-in tabbed browser with URL entry, bookmarks, and a one-press switch to the system browser

Cheap LFS restore shows a detailed progress card with the current and prefetched downloads, file and byte totals, transfer rate, estimated time remaining, and a cancel action

Ignored files such as node_modules, virtual environments or large checkpoints can be moved into a new local submodule, with every copy verified before the original repository is touched
The documentation site is now organized into tabs with a search field, plain-text or regular-expression matching, and the regex builder available on every tab
The app window paints immediately at launch, scanning for installed external editors in the background and loading heavy repository tabs only when they are opened
Cloud compression on a private repository no longer runs on that repository's own Actions minutes and no longer publishes its name or file paths

The two funny-level sliders now sit in Appearance beside the language mode with a live preview for each language, instead of being filed under Sound
A failed push, force push, pull or fetch reports the actual error instead of a generic notice saying a background action stopped unexpectedly

Settings > Git shows a visible label above the email box when no account is signed in, instead of an unlabelled field under Name
Diagrams on the documentation site render as pictures in both light and dark themes instead of shipping as raw diagram source
The documentation search page no longer freezes the tab on a slow or malicious regular expression, evaluating patterns in a background worker with a hard deadline
Right-clicking a folder in Windows Explorer offers Desktop Material entries, appearing in the top-level Windows 11 menu on packaged builds
A GitHub Packages explorer browses packages and versions and transfers files to and from a repository's container registry

The Repository Tools tracked-content search supports the shared filter modes, a case toggle, and the full regex builder
Signing in to an additional account is kept instead of being silently dropped and gone again on the next launch

Pushing works when the unpushed commits include a merge commit, instead of failing with a non-linear history error

Large-file uploads and probes confirm the remote first, so a renamed or transferred repository is never pushed to its old address
The version history search bar shows its filter mode controls and regex builder like every other search bar
Text no longer clips in the conflict banner, long Actions log lines scroll horizontally, and the filtered empty state stops covering Clear filters
Searching no longer pauses with a slow-pattern warning after a momentary stall, and never warns during plain-text search

Installed apps keep receiving updates when a push lands while a release is still building
Times display in 24-hour format by default, with the 12-hour choice still available in Date and time settings
Long lists in History, Actions, and Releases scroll and filter smoothly in large repositories
The notification centre, large TGA image previews, and streaming Ollama chat replies no longer freeze the window while they work
Large files upload in 500 MiB parts, so a dropped transfer retries far less data and progress updates more often
Pinning and committing large files finishes noticeably faster, especially with many files at once
Cancelling a package upload or download restores the transfer controls instead of leaving them stuck

Long-running operations such as history deepening, tag pushes, bulk branch deletion, bisect, subtree splits, and batch cloning show a progress bar and status instead of appearing frozen

Run a repository's GitHub Actions workflows on your own machine with act and Docker, including streaming logs, dispatch inputs, per-run secrets, a dry run and cancel

Repository tabs can be collected into named, colored groups that collapse behind a chip, stay together when the strip is sorted, and survive a restart

The Ollama model manager, the Copilot providers settings tab, and the background action queue can be found by name in the command palette

The documentation site gains a sticky search field wired to the regex builder and a collapsible menu on narrow screens
